title: Protocol negotiation and schema deprecation plan for telemetry SDK/CLI/API
creator: Maya Singh
description: We need a robust protocol negotiation layer and controlled deprecation process for telemetry schema versions across SDK, CLI, and API ingestion endpoints. This ticket codifies the runtime handshake, server-side compatibility rules, schema registry behavior, deprecation cadence, and analytics pipeline transforms required to safely introduce schema v2 while preserving ingestion for older clients and maintaining accurate usage analytics. The goal is zero-surprise rollouts for customers, clear roll-forward/fallback behavior in the face of incompatible clients, and measurable metrics for monitoring telemetry fidelity during the transition.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry ingestion endpoints accept an explicit 'X-Telemetry-Schema' header and negotiate to the highest mutually supported schema version
Server implements a schema registry with explicit compatibility rules (backward-compatible / non-breaking changes allowed; breaking changes flagged and gated)
SDKs and CLI are updated to include a version negotiation shim; older clients default to server-declared safe fallback behavior
Analytics pipeline has transformation steps to normalize v1 and v2 events and a join key to detect mixed-version traffic
Rollout plan documented with canary percentages, automated fallback on error-rate or parsing-failure thresholds, and a monitoring dashboard
End-to-end test harness that simulates mixed-version traffic and verifies metrics, failures, and deprecation warnings
tasks: Design endpoint negotiation spec (header names, payload flags, explicit schema version field)
Build schema registry service to store schemas, compatibility rules, and deprecation metadata
Add server-side middleware to read negotiation header, validate payload against chosen schema, and emit parse-failure events to monitoring
Extend SDK/CLI to send preferred schema versions and fall back on server policy; include clear deprecation warnings in logs
Create analytics pipeline converters that map old event fields to v2 canonical names and populate a 'telemetry_schema_version' field
Instrument dashboards and alerts: parse_fail_rate, normalized_event_ratio, downstream_metrics_consistency
Run a 2-week canary with 1%, 10%, 50% phases and predefined rollback criteria
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Older clients may send malformed events that bypass validation and skew analytics. Mitigation: Strict server-side validation with 'reject' policy in canary phases and 'log-and-accept' in initial slow rollout
Risk: Analytics joins break when fields rename. Mitigation: Pipeline converters and field-mapping tables in registry; add synthetic events to validate mapping
Risk: Increased latency from schema validation. Mitigation: Optimize validation path (compiled validators), async validation for non-critical fields, and measure p50/p95 during canary
Risk: Customers on private deployments cannot upgrade quickly. Mitigation: Provide compatibility shim option and clear deprecation timelines in release notes and console banners
rollout_plan_summary: Phase 0: internal testing and synthetic traffic. Phase 1: 1% canary for hosted API with 'reject' policy and alerting. Phase 2: 10% canary, switch to 'log-and-accept' for non-blocking fields. Phase 3: 50% canary with customer notifications. Phase 4: general availability with 90 day deprecation window for v1. Automated rollback triggers on sustained parse_fail_rate > 0.5% or transform_error increase > 3x baseline.
notes: Prefer header-based negotiation to payload nesting to keep client changes minimal
Registry should expose a human-readable deprecation_reason and suggested migration mapping
Consider embedding a compact compatibility bitmap in responses so SDKs can optimize behavior without repeated RTT
Align deprecation timeline with Dedicated/Private support team to ensure customers on reserved capacity are notified
